name: Gather Victim Identity Information
usage: Curates target lists of diplomats, political-party staffers and cybersecurity personnel via LinkedIn and public disclosure filings before phishing waves and password-spray campaigns.

name: Active Scanning
usage: Actively scans for exposed VPN and email-gateway appliances (Pulse Secure, Fortinet, Citrix, Exchange) prior to exploitation for initial access â documented in the joint CISA/NCSC 2021 advisory.

name: Acquire Infrastructure: Domains
usage: Registers vendor-lookalike domains and abuses compromised legitimate infrastructure â including trojanising SolarWinds Orion update servers â to blend C2 into expected traffic.

name: Develop Capabilities: Malware
usage: Continuously develops bespoke tooling: SUNBURST/TEARDROP/GoldMax in the SolarWinds era; ROOTSAW dropper and WINELOADER modular backdoor in 2023-2024 diplomatic campaigns.

name: Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
usage: Signature technique: trojanised SolarWinds Orion updates (SUNBURST) reached approximately 18,000 downstream customer environments in 2020, giving APT29 access to select federal and private-sector targets.

name: Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts
usage: Preferred 2023-2024 initial access: abuses long-lived service-principal credentials, dormant test accounts and stolen refresh tokens to log directly into Microsoft 365 / Entra ID â used against HPE and Microsoft's own tenant.

name: Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment
usage: WINELOADER campaigns deliver ROOTSAW/HTA droppers via PDF invitations themed as political dinners, ambassador receptions or NATO briefings against CDU, foreign ministries and think tanks.

name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
usage: Documented in the 2021 joint CISA/NCSC advisory exploiting known CVEs in Pulse Secure Connect (CVE-2019-11510), Fortinet FortiGate (CVE-2018-13379), Citrix ADC (CVE-2019-19781) and VMware Workspace ONE (CVE-2020-4006).

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
usage: PowerShell Empire and bespoke PowerShell one-liners are used across intrusions, including the 2018 US think-tank campaign and hands-on-keyboard SolarWinds follow-on operations.

name: Account Manipulation: Device Registration
usage: As Midnight Blizzard, registers rogue devices for MFA on compromised accounts to maintain persistent tenant access after credential compromise â highlighted by CISA in AA24-057A.

name: Create Account: Cloud Account
usage: Creates malicious OAuth applications and grants them elevated Graph API permissions on compromised tenants â the pivot from the Microsoft test tenant into corporate mailboxes in November 2023.

name: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token
usage: Steals and reuses OAuth refresh tokens and application access tokens harvested from compromised endpoints and mailboxes to bypass MFA and maintain quiet residency in M365 / Azure environments.

name: Obfuscated Files or Information
usage: SUNBURST hides malicious code inside a legitimate SolarWinds DLL with delayed activation, blocklist domains, and jitter to evade sandboxing. HAMMERTOSS previously used steganography over Twitter for C2.

name: Brute Force: Password Spraying
usage: Initial access vector for the Microsoft November 2023 compromise: a low-and-slow password spray of a legacy non-production tenant that lacked MFA. CISA AA24-057A calls out password spraying as a defining SVR technique.

name: Steal Application Access Token
usage: Consented malicious OAuth apps and stolen refresh tokens are harvested to survive password resets and to move from user impersonation to full mailbox reads via the Microsoft Graph API.

name: Cloud Service Discovery
usage: Enumerates Azure/Entra ID tenants, service principals, Microsoft Graph permissions and mailbox delegation before pivoting â documented in Mandiant's 2022 Microsoft 365 write-up.

name: Email Collection: Remote Email Collection
usage: Primary collection objective in the Microsoft, HPE and diplomatic campaigns: bulk read of executive and cybersecurity-staff mailboxes via Exchange Online / Microsoft Graph after obtaining an app or delegated token.

name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
usage: HTTPS beacons to attacker-controlled infrastructure, historically via Sunburst's DNS/HTTPS mix, and more recently via long-poll Graph API and OAuth flows that blend into normal M365 traffic.

name: Web Service
usage: Long-running preference for legitimate cloud services as C2: Twitter and steganographic images (HAMMERTOSS, 2015), GitHub Gists (Duke era), Google Drive and Dropbox (2022 diplomatic campaigns), Trello (2020 phishing).

name: Exfiltration Over Web Service: Cloud Storage
usage: Mailbox contents and internal documents are exfiltrated to attacker-controlled Dropbox and Google Drive accounts or bounced through the same Graph API endpoints used for C2, minimising anomalous egress.

name: Phishing: Spearphishing Link
usage: Bit.ly-shortened links to credential-harvesting pages spoofing Google, Microsoft and government webmail â the exact technique used against Podesta in March 2016 and against the Biden campaign in 2020 (ZIRCONIUM operation named by Google TAG).

name: Drive-by Compromise
usage: Strategic web compromises of policy think-tank and government sites (e.g. 2015 activity chronicled by Kaspersky) using browser exploits and Sedkit / Sednit exploit kit landing pages.

name: Forced Authentication
usage: Core to APT28's 2022-2024 credential-theft campaigns: Outlook CVE-2023-23397 uses the PidLidReminderFileParameter property in a calendar item to force the victim client to authenticate to an attacker-controlled SMB share, leaking Net-NTLMv2 hashes without user interaction.

name: User Execution: Malicious File
usage: Sofacy documents rely on the target enabling macros or opening an embedded object; Sedreco / JHUHUGIT / Zebrocy droppers frequently disguise themselves as PDFs, HTA files or LNKs.

name: Scheduled Task/Job: Scheduled Task
usage: APT28 uses schtasks and the Task Scheduler to persist X-Agent, Zebrocy and Cannon droppers on victim endpoints.

name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
usage: Persistence for X-Agent, Zebrocy and Sedreco via HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run entries and the Startup folder.

name: Pre-OS Boot: Bootkit / UEFI Rootkit
usage: LoJax â the first UEFI rootkit found in the wild â was deployed by APT28/Sednit against Balkan government targets to survive OS reinstallation and disk replacement.

name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
usage: GooseEgg exploits Windows Print Spooler CVE-2022-38028 to run privileged code and dump credentials on domain controllers; earlier campaigns exploited CVE-2015-1701, CVE-2015-2387 and CVE-2017-0263.

name: Valid Accounts
usage: Post-credential-theft, APT28 pivots into victim environments using stolen usernames and passwords â the object of its long-running password-spraying and NTLM-relay campaigns.

name: OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory
usage: Dumps LSASS via Mimikatz-style tools and GooseEgg's spooler-triggered code execution to obtain Kerberos tickets and NTLM hashes for lateral movement.

name: Input Capture: Keylogging
usage: X-Agent implements a plug-in keylogger for Windows, Linux, macOS and Android; used to capture Bundestag and DNC user credentials and against Ukrainian artillery officers via the Android CHOPSTICK variant.

name: Proxy: Multi-hop Proxy
usage: X-Tunnel provides encrypted TCP relaying and pivoting between the operator and X-Agent implants inside victim networks â used for both the DNC intrusion and multiple Ukrainian government engagements.

name: Ingress Tool Transfer
usage: First-stage downloaders (Seduploader, Zebrocy, HeadLace) pull second-stage X-Agent modules and post-compromise tooling from staging infrastructure.

name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
usage: Both X-Agent and Zebrocy compress and beacon staged data back over the same HTTP/HTTPS channel used for command-and-control.

name: Gather Victim Identity Information: Email Addresses
usage: Curates target rosters at aerospace, defence and cryptocurrency employers from LinkedIn and industry directories before Dream Job lures.

name: Establish Accounts: Social Media Accounts
usage: Maintains long-lived LinkedIn recruiter personae (Boeing, Lockheed, Coinbase, Meta) that build trust over weeks before pushing a trojanised coding challenge.

name: Phishing: Spearphishing via Service
usage: Primary access vector: LinkedIn / WhatsApp recruiter DMs handing over trojanised PDF briefs or Windows-only "assessment" archives.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: JavaScript
usage: Bybit intrusion (Feb 2025) executed as target-scoped malicious JavaScript injected into the Safe{Wallet} front-end, rewriting a routine multisig transaction on the fly.

name: Hijack Execution Flow: DLL Side-Loading
usage: Signed-executable DLL side-loading is a house tradecraft: TAXHAUL/COLDCAT in the 3CX chain, MagicRAT/QuiteRAT loaders in the 2023 energy-sector campaigns, and MISTPEN in Dream Job.

name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
usage: FudModule 1.x/2.x kernel rootkit patches out EDR-hook callbacks and blinds ETW providers; the 3.1 variant (2026) additionally toggles Smart App Control off from kernel space.

name: Subvert Trust Controls: Code Signing
usage: 3CXDesktopApp and X_TRADER installers were signed with legitimate publisher certificates before being pushed to the update channel; MagicRAT loaders reuse leaked NVIDIA certificates.

name: System Information Discovery
usage: MISTPEN, MagicRAT and BLINDINGCAN all fingerprint host OS build, architecture, domain and installed AV before staging the next payload.

name: Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
usage: ThreatNeedle intrusions used SMB and admin shares plus purpose-built router-side tunnels to bridge segmented IT/OT networks in defence targets.

name: Encrypted Channel: Asymmetric Cryptography
usage: AppleJeus and BLINDINGCAN wrap their command channel in an RSA-then-AES envelope pinned to a per-victim key baked into the loader.

name: Data Destruction
usage: Destover wiper (Sony 2014), DarkSeoul / Jokra (South Korea 2013) and the Wipe stage of WannaCry (2017) all belong to Lazarus' destructive playbook.

name: Financial Theft
usage: Bangladesh Bank SWIFT ($81M, 2016), Ronin bridge ($625M, 2022), Bybit cold wallet ($1.5B, 2025) and sustained ATM cash-out (FASTCash) are the group's revenue-generating end objective.

name: Obtain Capabilities: Vulnerabilities
usage: Consistent pattern of weaponising n-days within hours of PoC release (Citrix, Cisco, Zoho, Log4Shell) and holding at least one zero-day (USAHerds CVE-2021-44207).

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
usage: install.bat creates the StoreSyncSvc service and registers the DLL; APT41 uses cmd.exe heavily for reconnaissance and lateral movement.

name: Windows Management Instrumentation
usage: APT41 uses WMI for both execution and remote system enumeration during post-compromise lateral movement.

name: Hijack Execution Flow: DLL Side-Loading
usage: Long-running staple: DUSTPAN and DUSTTRAP, Zscaler's DodgeBox loader, StealthVector/StealthReacher (Earth Baku) â legitimate signed executables side-load malicious DLLs.

name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
usage: install.bat creates 'StoreSyncSvc' pointing at storesyncsvc.dll for BEACON persistence; DEADEYE variants (state-government campaign) also persist as services.

name: Masquerading: Task or Service
usage: Malicious service names impersonate legitimate Windows components (StoreSyncSvc, svchost hosting) to blend into host telemetry.

name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Software Packing
usage: VMProtect-packed Meterpreter loaders (2.exe) in 2020 campaigns; DEADEYE variants use VMProtect and ConfuserEx obfuscation in the state-government intrusions.

name: Indicator Removal: File Deletion
usage: APT41 removes staged loaders and tooling after execution to hinder DFIR â a documented ATT&CK-linked TTP for the group.

name: Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol
usage: RDP is APT41's preferred lateral-movement channel once valid credentials are in hand, per MITRE and Mandiant IR observations.

name: Web Service: Dead Drop Resolver
usage: TOUGHPROGRESS stores encrypted commands and exfiltrated data inside Google Calendar event descriptions, using Google infrastructure as a dead drop.

name: Data Encrypted for Impact
usage: Financially motivated wing of APT41 has deployed ransomware (Encryptor RaaS) against gaming and technology victims; MITRE credits T1486 to G0096.

name: Stage Capabilities: Upload Malware
usage: Hosts MSIX App-Installer packages, PowerShell loaders and NetSupport RAT payloads on attacker-controlled and lookalike-brand domains before Google Ads-driven traffic delivery.

name: Replication Through Removable Media
usage: Mailed BadUSB drives, configured as HID keyboards, sent to US defence, transport and insurance firms starting August 2021 (FBI PIN, January 2022). Drives auto-injected PowerShell to install Metasploit/Cobalt Strike and drop BlackMatter or REvil.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Visual Basic
usage: VBS/VBA macros inside weaponised Office documents were the workhorse in the 2015-2018 POS-malware campaigns; also used in Bateleur JavaScript-loader chains.

name: Event Triggered Execution: Application Shimming
usage: Signature FIN7 persistence trick: registered Windows Application Compatibility shim databases to reinject Carbanak/GRIFFON into legitimate processes at reboot.

name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Command Obfuscation
usage: POWERTRASH is heavily obfuscated (concatenated strings, char-code encoding, junk code) to defeat PowerShell logging and static AV signatures.

name: Reflective Code Loading
usage: POWERTRASH reflectively loads the Lizar/DICELOADER DLL entirely in memory; the 2025 Anubis Python backdoor also uses in-memory DLL loading.

name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Bypass User Account Control
usage: MITRE lists UAC bypass among FIN7's staples for elevating Carbanak/Lizar loaders on standard-user hosts.

name: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Kerberoasting
usage: Standard part of FIN7's post-exploitation kit alongside Mimikatz for offline cracking of service-account credentials before ransomware detonation.

name: Remote Access Tools
usage: NetSupport RAT is FIN7's/GrayAlpha's primary hands-on remote access tool in 2023-2026, delivered via MSIX and fake browser updates; Atera has also been observed in earlier ransomware precursor stages.

name: Video Capture
usage: Carbanak's most distinctive feature: a real-time desktop video-recording module used to observe operator workflows inside banks before executing money-mules or SWIFT transfers.

name: Exploitation of Remote Services
usage: Exploited EternalBlue/EternalRomance (MS17-010) in NotPetya, PrintNightmare and Follina in 2022 Ukraine ops, and MikroTik/ASUS router firmware in VPNFilter/Cyclops Blink.

name: Inhibit System Recovery
usage: Wipers delete Volume Shadow Copies and overwrite the MBR/VBR (NotPetya, HermeticWiper-family, CaddyWiper) to prevent restore-from-image or bootloader recovery.

name: Disk Wipe: Disk Structure Wipe
usage: NotPetya, Olympic Destroyer, SwiftSlicer and AcidRain destroy MBR/partition tables and, for AcidRain, wipe SurfBeam2 modem flash and MTD devices to brick hardware.

name: Firmware Corruption
usage: AcidRain (Viasat KA-SAT SurfBeam2 modems, Feb 2022) and VPNFilter's 'dstr' plugin (2018) overwrite persistent firmware/flash so devices become unusable.

name: ICS: Manipulation of Control
usage: Industroyer (2016) and Industroyer2 (2022) natively speak IEC-101/IEC-104/IEC 61850/OPC DA to open substation breakers and manipulate protection relays.

name: Trusted Relationship
usage: Signature Cloud Hopper tradecraft: compromise Managed Service Providers and use their trusted, credentialled access to pivot into client networks worldwide.

name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Encrypted/Encoded File
usage: Ecipekac hides encrypted shellcodes inside digitally signed DLLs preserving signature validity; LODEINFO variants use XOR/base64 layered encoding.

name: Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information
usage: Loaders (NOOPLDR, Ecipekac, DOWNIISSA) decrypt AES/XOR-encrypted payloads at runtime; NOOPLDR keys decryption to the host's MachineId + ComputerName.

name: OS Credential Dumping: NTDS
usage: Deploys ntdsutil and Impacket secretsdump.py against domain controllers, then archives NTDS.dit for exfiltration.

name: OS Credential Dumping: SAM
usage: Uses Mimikatz and PwDump against local SAM to harvest admin credentials for MSP-to-client pivoting.

name: Archive Collected Data: Archive via Utility
usage: Compresses staged data with RAR/TAR before exfil, frequently splitting archives to evade DLP; stages under Recycle Bin paths.

name: Dynamic Resolution: Fast Flux DNS
usage: Historic use of fast-flux DNS for RedLeaves and PlugX C2 infrastructure; NOOPDOOR uses DGA-based C2 name resolution.

name: Permission Groups Discovery: Domain Groups
usage: AdFind, ADRecon and BloodHound were used to enumerate Active Directory groups and identify domain-admin paths.

name: Acquire Infrastructure: Virtual Private Server
usage: Signs up Azure App Service and Azure Storage tenants under fraudulent Microsoft accounts to host Tickler C2 and staging; also used private VPS hosts to fan out obfuscated command-and-control layers documented by Trend Micro in 2019.

name: Office Application Startup: Office Test
usage: HOLMIUM-era operations abused the SensePost 'Ruler' technique to plant malicious Outlook home-page rules that ran VBScript on mailbox open â an Exchange-native persistence and execution primitive.

name: Credentials from Password Stores
usage: Post-authentication use of AzureHound and Roadtools to enumerate Entra ID and pull cloud-service secrets after successful spray hits.

name: Account Discovery: Cloud Account
usage: AzureHound and Roadtools enumeration of Entra ID users, groups and service principals immediately after cloud-account takeover.

name: Supply Chain Compromise
usage: Documented use of compromised third-party organisations (IT service providers, HR portals, an Israeli job-board) as beachheads to reach the intended government or telecom target.

name: Exploitation for Client Execution
usage: Weaponised CVE-2017-11882 (Office Equation Editor) within days of the November 2017 patch to drop POWRUNER / BONDUPDATER on Middle Eastern government targets.

name: Server Software Component: Web Shell
usage: TwoFace, RGDoor (native IIS module) and Veaty passive IIS backdoors give redundant access to internet-facing web servers even after other backdoors are burned.

name: Office Application Startup: Outlook Home Page
usage: Abuses the Outlook Home Page feature to load attacker-controlled HTA content when the mailbox is opened â a hallmark OilRig persistence primitive.

name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Compiled HTML File
usage: CHM (compiled help) files carry embedded scripts that invoke PowerShell/VBScript â a favoured OilRig LOLBin technique to bypass macro warnings and AV baselines.

name: Modify Authentication Process: Password Filter DLL
usage: In Earth Simnavaz, a password-filter DLL was registered on domain controllers to capture cleartext credentials at password-change events, then exfiltrated via Exchange (StealHook).

name: Application Layer Protocol: DNS
usage: Signature OilRig tradecraft: DNS-tunnel C2 across Helminth, ISMAgent, ALMA Communicator, BONDUPDATER (TXT records), QUADAGENT (AAAA queries) and Saitama (finite-state DNS machine); resurfaces in 2024 Spearal against Iraq.

name: Protocol Tunneling
usage: Plink is repeatedly used to open reverse SSH tunnels from compromised hosts, then RDP inbound through the tunnel â visible in Fox Kitten, Crambus and 2024 Iraq campaigns.

name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
usage: Data is exfiltrated over the same DNS or Exchange-mail channels used for C2 rather than opening a new outbound socket â StealHook writes stolen credentials into Exchange mail, Saitama exfils over DNS queries.

name: Process Injection
usage: Bluenoroff / APT38 implants (DYEPACK, MACKTRUCK, Manuscrypt) inject shellcode and DLLs into legitimate processes (svchost.exe, explorer.exe) to hide from EDR on SWIFT and cryptocurrency-exchange operator workstations.

name: Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files
usage: In cryptocurrency intrusions (Ronin, Bybit, WazirX) operators harvest wallet seed phrases, private keys and cloud-console tokens from developer workstations, browser storage and .env / config files after the initial macOS/Windows compromise.

name: Phishing for Information: Spearphishing Link
usage: Sends tailored benign emails with web-beacon-instrumented links and credential-harvesting pages to profile targets before deploying malware; Proofpoint (Feb 2024) observed a shift to embedded tracking pixels.

name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Mshta
usage: Macro-based lures invoke mshta.exe to fetch and run HTA payloads that stage AppleSeed/BabyShark. Kaspersky's GoldDragon writeup shows the exact mshta chain fingerprinted by victim IP.

name: External Remote Services
usage: Custom RDP Wrapper builds and a modified TeamViewer client used to keep hands-on-keyboard access; 2025 AhnLab reporting shows the shift from bespoke backdoors to RDP-based persistence.

name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Name or Location
usage: TRANSLATEXT masquerades as Google Translate; installers imitate South Korean groupware (Gomir); JS/VBS droppers open a legitimate decoy document so the user sees the expected content.

name: Credentials from Password Stores: Credentials from Web Browsers
usage: TRANSLATEXT harvests Gmail/Naver/Kakao/Daum credentials; forceCopy (2025) copies browser Local State + Login Data files to steal cookies and stored passwords while bypassing on-write EDR hooks.

name: Screen Capture
usage: TRANSLATEXT captures browser screenshots every 5 seconds; AppleSeed and Troll Stealer both include screenshot modules exfiltrated over HTTP/SMTP.

name: Develop Capabilities: Code Signing Certificates
usage: Historically signed droppers and Retro backdoor components with stolen or forged code-signing certificates from Deutsche Telekom, Digisign, TechnoTrust and Cyberoam to defeat Windows trust warnings.

name: Adversary-in-the-Middle
usage: Hotel Wi-Fi campaigns positioned the operator between the target and legitimate update servers to substitute signed update binaries in transit.

name: Masquerading
usage: Fake update prompts imitate legitimate Adobe Flash, Google Toolbar and Windows Messenger installers, complete with valid-looking icons and metadata.

name: Data from Local System
usage: Ramsay collects Word (.doc/.docx) and PDF files from local storage; Retro/Tapaoux collect email, IM history and browser data on compromised executive endpoints.

name: Acquire Infrastructure: Web Services
usage: Turla routinely stages C2 on legitimate web services (Dropbox for Crutch, WordPress-based watering holes, hijacked satellite downlinks, expired Andromeda C2 domains).

name: Compromise Infrastructure: Botnet
usage: Hijacked expired Andromeda (Gamarue) C2 domains in 2022 to selectively re-task existing bots for espionage against Ukrainian targets â first publicly documented case of one APT taking over another's live botnet.

name: Rootkit
usage: Snake / Uroburos is a modular kernel-mode rootkit that intercepts I/O, hides files and processes, and maintains a peer-to-peer C2 mesh across compromised hosts.

name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Rundll32
usage: TinyTurla and Carbon are frequently loaded via rundll32.exe with exported entry points disguised as legitimate Windows DLL functions.

name: Application Layer Protocol: Mail Protocols
usage: LightNeuron and LunarMail use SMTP/IMAP as the C2 transport â LightNeuron parses steganographic PDF/JPG attachments as they flow through Microsoft Exchange, and LunarMail uses Outlook add-in email attachments for tasking.

name: Web Service: Bidirectional Communication
usage: ComRAT v4 uses Gmail's web interface as a bidirectional C2 channel; Crutch uses Dropbox for tasking and exfiltration.

name: Traffic Signaling
usage: Turla pioneered hijacking of one-way satellite internet downlinks: implants sent traffic to the spoofed IP address of a legitimate satellite subscriber so the operator received C2 responses over a satellite feed without ever exposing an attacker-owned server.

name: Stage Capabilities: Drive-by Target
usage: Compromises legitimate ASEAN news, government and NGO sites and injects OceanLotus profiling scripts to fingerprint and selectively redirect visitors.

name: Data from Information Repositories
usage: Extracts data from Global Address Lists and SharePoint / Exchange information repositories reachable from a compromised mailbox; as Silk Typhoon extends this to SaaS repositories reached through stolen tokens.

name: Data Staged: Remote Data Staging
usage: Stages archives on a compromised host (often the Exchange server itself) inside publicly reachable directories, then downloads them via the web shell.

name: Network Service Discovery
usage: Runs internal port and share enumeration from the initial Exchange foothold using nltest, net.exe and Impacket variants to map the target Active Directory environment.

name: Acquire Infrastructure: Botnet
usage: Operates the KV Botnet, a covert relay layer of end-of-life Cisco RV, DrayTek Vigor and NETGEAR ProSAFE SOHO routers, to originate traffic from residential IP space inside the victim country and blend into normal network noise.

name: Valid Accounts: Domain Accounts
usage: Prefers standing domain accounts and elevated administrator credentials for post-exploitation to reduce reliance on new malware.

name: System Binary Proxy Execution
usage: Signature Living-off-the-Land approach: heavy reliance on signed built-in Windows binaries (wmic, ntdsutil, netsh, cmd, PowerShell) to avoid dropping bespoke malware onto disk.

name: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Pass the Hash
usage: Moves laterally within Active Directory environments by re-using stolen NTLM hashes rather than cracking passwords, again to avoid alerting on interactive logons.

name: Unsecured Credentials: Private Keys
usage: Extracts SSH keys and other private-key material from compromised hosts and stolen backups to enable authenticated pivoting through the environment.

name: Account Discovery
usage: Enumerates local and domain accounts with net user, net group, whoami and nltest /domain_trusts to map privilege paths inside Active Directory.

name: Archive Collected Data
usage: Compresses staged files with archivers such as WinRAR or 7-Zip prior to exfiltration to reduce volume and disguise sensitive content as routine archives.

name: Data Staged
usage: Stages collected files under masqueraded paths on domain controllers or file servers before archiving and exfiltrating, taking advantage of legitimate administrative shares.

name: Indicator Removal: Clear Windows Event Logs
usage: Clears Security, System and PowerShell event logs with wevtutil cl and Clear-EventLog to erase evidence of ntdsutil and LSASS access.

name: Compromise Accounts: Email Accounts
usage: Uses legitimate compromised diplomat mailboxes to launch onward phishing at NATO and EU foreign ministries â most visibly in the February 2022 TA416 wave immediately after the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

name: Obfuscated Files or Information: HTML Smuggling
usage: SmugX (2023) embeds the PlugX loader inside an HTML document that reconstructs a ZIP/LNK on the client, bypassing perimeter file-type filters.

name: File and Directory Discovery
usage: PUBLOAD, DOPLUGS and PlugX enumerate document trees for keyword-matching filenames (Ukraine, ASEAN, Vatican, refugee, ministry) before staging.

name: Exfiltration Over Physical Medium: USB
usage: Custom PlugX variants copy sensitive documents onto attached USB drives â an air-gap-jumping capability specifically cited in the DoJ affidavit and in Check Point's WispRider analysis.

name: Encrypted Channel: Symmetric Cryptography
usage: RC4-encrypted PlugX payloads and configuration blocks; MQsTTang encrypts its MQTT topic payloads with a per-victim key.

name: Compromise Infrastructure: Network Devices
usage: Camaro Dragon's Horse Shell malicious firmware implant compromises TP-Link SOHO routers to relay C2 traffic transparently from operator to victim.

name: Active Scanning: Vulnerability Scanning
usage: Runs Acunetix and bespoke scanners against victims' public-facing servers to find exploitable ProxyShell, GlassFish and other web-service flaws before intrusion.

name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Print Processors
usage: Registers a malicious spool.dll under 'HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Control\Print\Environments\Windows x64\Print Processors\UDPrint' so the Print Spooler service side-loads the payload on service restart - the same trick documented in ESET's PipeMon research.

name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Steganography
usage: Hides shellcode inside a BMP image file for later decoding by a bespoke loader, a technique tied to the FunnySwitch and Cobalt Strike loader families.

name: OS Credential Dumping: DCSync
usage: Runs 'mimikatz lsadump::dcsync' against a compromised domain controller to pull Kerberos long-term secrets from Active Directory replication.

name: Remote System Discovery
usage: Enumerates network hosts through a PowerShell 'Get-EventLog -LogName security' one-liner that filters Event ID 4624 logons for source addresses, plus a suite of open-source scanners.

name: Proxy
usage: Fronts compromised web servers with Cloudflare so the beacon and C2 traffic ride the CDN's TLS certificate and IP space, obscuring the operator origin.

name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Shortcut Modification
usage: PipeMon persists by dropping a shortcut into the Print Processors path so it is loaded by spoolsv.exe at logon.

name: Process Injection: Dynamic-link Library Injection
usage: PipeMon and later Winnti loaders inject DLLs into privileged processes to escalate and to hide payloads.

name: Execution Guardrails: Environmental Keying
usage: In ShadowHammer, the second-stage payload was gated by a hard-coded list of ~600 target MAC addresses; unmatched hosts received only a benign stub.

name: Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion: System Checks
usage: PipeMon and Winnti check for VM artefacts and analyst tools before executing further stages.

name: Software Discovery: Security Software Discovery
usage: Enumerates installed AV/EDR before dropping the kernel driver, dropping bespoke shims for hosts running Kaspersky or Chinese domestic AV.

name: Exploitation for Defense Evasion
usage: GrayFish's kernel components exploited undocumented Windows APIs to disable security-driver callbacks and to hide the encrypted virtual file system from user-mode inspection.

name: Pre-OS Boot: System Firmware
usage: Signature capability: the nls_933w.dll module reflashed hard-drive firmware on at least twelve vendors (Seagate, WD, Samsung, Toshiba, IBM, Micron, Hitachi and others) to create a persistence store that survived OS reinstall and disk formatting.

name: Establish Accounts: Email Accounts
usage: TA453 multi-persona operations: several attacker-controlled Gmail / ProtonMail accounts injected into the same thread to lend social proof to a fake conference or interview invite.

name: User Execution: Malicious Link
usage: Victims click phishing links leading to fake conference or interview pages that harvest credentials or serve archive-based loaders.

name: Automated Collection
usage: HYPERSCRAPE fully automates mailbox iteration, EML download and cleanup of Google security-alert emails so the victim never sees the login notification.

name: Non-Application Layer Protocol
usage: Distinctive PingPull capability: ICMP-tunnelled C2 that hides command traffic inside ping echo-request/reply payloads, useful on carrier networks that permit ICMP but restrict HTTP egress.

name: Proxy: External Proxy
usage: HTRAN and SoftEther VPN clients are used as intermediary hop points to disguise operator IPs; SoftEther is deployed on compromised jump hosts inside victim networks.

name: Create Account: Local Account
usage: NICKEL operations created local accounts on compromised hosts to survive credential rotation on the primary victim identity.

name: Access Token Manipulation
usage: APT15 has manipulated access tokens to escalate from a user context to SYSTEM during NICKEL post-exploitation, per MSTIC's write-up.

name: System Network Configuration Discovery
usage: Uses ipconfig, netstat, arp and route to fingerprint compromised hosts â documented across BS2005, RoyalCLI and Ketrican operations.

name: Account Discovery: Domain Account
usage: APT15 enumerates domain users and admin groups (net user, net group /domain) before selecting lateral-movement targets.

name: Email Collection: Local Email Collection
usage: NCC Group observed APT15 extracting Exchange mailbox content from the UK contractor's on-prem Exchange server, using the spwebmember utility and its own Exchange enumeration tooling.

name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution
usage: Registry Run keys used by SslMM and WinMM to survive reboots on compromised government workstations.

name: Office Application Startup: Add-ins
usage: Office application add-ins used as a persistence mechanism observed by Kaspersky in the MsnMM cluster.

name: Develop Capabilities: Digital Certificates
usage: Generates self-signed and Let's Encrypt TLS certificates for short-lived C2 hostnames on Cloudflare tunnel and Workers infrastructure.

name: Office Application Startup
usage: Long-standing use of Office template injection and Normal.dotm modification so that opening any Word document re-executes Gamaredon's downloader.

name: Template Injection
usage: Documents fetch a remote Word template from Gamaredon-controlled infrastructure at open time, side-stepping static AV of the initial file.

name: Obtain Capabilities: Tool
usage: Bundles legitimate third-party tools inside its toolchain: Sysinternals PsExec for lateral movement, and the DiskCryptor open-source volume-encryption suite as the destructive core of DCSrv.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Python
usage: PyDCrypt is a Python-based launcher (PyInstaller-packed) that copies DCSrv to remote hosts, runs it and cleans up its own artefacts.

name: Modify Registry
usage: DCSrv writes to HKLM registry keys to install its service and to set boot-time flags for the DiskCryptor driver.

name: Lateral Tool Transfer
usage: PyDCrypt distributes DCSrv (dc.exe / dc.sys) to each remote host it targets, alongside the credentials needed to install and start the service.

name: System Shutdown/Reboot
usage: DCSrv forces a system reboot after installing the DiskCryptor driver so that the pre-boot encryption stage runs and denies further access to the host.

name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
usage: Ships archives out over PuTTY Secure Copy Protocol and WinSCP to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
usage: Runs a lightweight callback remote shell that connects to Whitefly infrastructure and waits for interactive commands; PowerShell scripts handle living-off-the-land steps once inside.

name: BITS Jobs
usage: BADNEWS variants have used Background Intelligent Transfer Service jobs to fetch payloads and beacon under legitimate Windows service cover.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Network Device CLI
usage: Runs commands directly on compromised Cisco IOS XE/NX-OS devices to alter configurations, enable GRE tunnels and stage packet captures.

name: Modify System Image: Patch System Image
usage: Modifies running Cisco device images and configurations to retain access, add unauthorized loopbacks and hide sub-interfaces used for tunnels.

name: Modify Authentication Process
usage: On compromised Cisco routers, alters AAA/TACACS configuration to accept attacker-supplied credentials and to log attacker sessions differently.

name: OS Credential Dumping
usage: Dumps LSASS, SAM and ntds.dit from compromised Windows infrastructure; extracts TACACS/RADIUS secrets from router configs to widen access across the carrier estate.

name: Unsecured Credentials
usage: Harvests weak-hash local device credentials, plain-text passwords from configuration files, and TACACS keys reused across the carrier fleet.

name: Remote Services
usage: Pivots between carrier assets over SSH, RDP and vendor-management protocols using stolen valid accounts; JumbledPath utility scripts the hop chain across routers.

name: Network Sniffing
usage: Enables SPAN/monitor sessions and full packet capture on compromised routers to record targeted call metadata, SMS content and lawful-intercept relay traffic.

name: Data from Configuration Repository
usage: Extracts full running-config and startup-config from compromised routers via SNMP and TFTP to obtain TACACS keys, ACL entries and lawful-intercept configuration.

name: Indicator Removal
usage: JumbledPath utility deletes device logs and rolls back configuration audit trails after each hop; on Windows hosts, clears event logs to hide GhostSpider stages.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
usage: Every published Rocke infection chain begins with a bash dropper that fetches the next stage from Pastebin/Gitee/CDN, sets cron persistence, kills rival miners and launches XMRig.

name: Scheduled Task/Job: Cron
usage: Canonical Rocke persistence: writes cron entries under /etc/cron.d, /var/spool/cron and per-user crontabs to reinstall the miner and re-fetch config from the current C2 every few minutes.

name: Create or Modify System Process: Systemd Service
usage: Later Rocke variants (2019 Go family, Pro-Ocean) install systemd unit files to run the miner as a boot-time service and restart it on kill.

name: Hijack Execution Flow: Dynamic Linker Hijacking
usage: Pro-Ocean's userland rootkit uses LD_PRELOAD (libprocesshider-style) to hook libc readdir / accept and hide the miner process and its sockets from ps, top, netstat and lsof.

name: Disable or Modify Tools
usage: The Rocke trademark: shell routines that specifically uninstall the Alibaba Cloud Aegis / aliyun cloud-monitor agent and Tencent Cloud YunJing / qcloud-monitor agent, plus killing common Linux AV daemons, before starting the miner. This is the case ATT&CK cites for cloud-agent tampering.

name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Compile After Delivery
usage: Rocke's 2019 Go family arrived as pre-compiled Go binaries stripped of symbols; earlier campaigns compiled ancillary components (kernel modules, small C helpers) on-host to defeat static hash detection.

name: Hide Artifacts: Hidden Files and Directories
usage: Miner binaries and staging scripts land under dot-prefixed directories (e.g. /tmp/.X-unix, /var/tmp/.systemd) to blend with legitimate hidden paths.

name: Remote Services: SSH
usage: Uses harvested SSH keys and dictionary-attacked passwords to spread the miner across reachable Linux hosts within the compromised network.

name: Resource Hijacking: Compute Hijacking
usage: The reason the group exists: illicit XMRig-based Monero mining against attacker-owned pools, running to full CPU on hijacked servers until removed or the pool wallet is rotated.

name: Process Injection: Proc Memory
usage: Writes shellcode directly to /proc/pid/mem of a spawned 'cat' process on Junos, overwriting the fclose GOT entry to redirect execution to the injected loader.

name: Subvert Trust Controls: Code Signing Policy Modification
usage: Bad VIB(E)s: crafted VIBs labelled PartnerSupported with empty signature files, XML acceptance-level manually flipped from community to partner, installed via `esxcli software vib install --force`.

name: Compromise Host Software Binary
usage: Backdoored /usr/bin/ssh and /usr/sbin/sshd log passwords XOR-encrypted with 0xEF; backdoored /usr/bin/tac_plus writes captured TACACS+ credentials. yum-versionlock pins the modified openssh packages.

name: Impair Defenses: Indicator Blocking
usage: BOLDMOVE patches Fortinet miglogd/syslogd across firmware versions; on Junos, lmpad rewrites snmpd (0x8601328) and mgd (0x84E90D8) function prologues to NOP audit and SNMP logging.

name: Indicator Removal: Clear Linux or Mac System Logs
usage: Deletes vmdird core dumps post-exploitation to hide CVE-2023-34048 crashes; sed/echo-clears Fortinet django.log and apache2 error logs; timestomps VIB install times before deploying malicious bundles.

name: Obtain Capabilities: Malware
usage: Acquired and deployed njRAT (MITRE S0385) alongside custom implants in the Log4Shell academic-institution intrusion.

name: Masquerading: Invalid Code Signature
usage: Loaders and installer stubs carry forged or invalid Authenticode signatures to slip past casual signature checks.

name: Peripheral Device Discovery
usage: Bespoke Bluetooth harvester (2019 Kaspersky report) enumerates paired devices; other modules inventory removable drives and printers.

name: Audio Capture
usage: M2RAT and Chinotto record microphone audio on demand â a distinguishing feature versus most other RGB implants.

name: Phishing (Mobile)
usage: Distributes Android surveillance apps (AndroRAT variants disguised as Islamic-prayer and Kashmir-news apps; the Dracarys trojanised Signal clone) via smishing and typosquatted download pages.

name: Inter-Process Communication: Dynamic Data Exchange
usage: Uses Microsoft Office DDE to execute embedded commands in Word documents delivered as spearphishing lures, seen in Cisco Talos's 2022 Bangladeshi military campaign.

name: Encrypted Channel
usage: Wraps HTTP beacons in Let's Encrypt-issued TLS certificates; MiyaRAT additionally applies an AES layer over payload bodies before sending them over TLS.

name: Dynamic Resolution
usage: Historic reliance on free dynamic-DNS services documented by Forcepoint in 2016; MITRE retains the technique on the current G1002 mapping.

name: Data from Removable Media
usage: USBWorm collects documents from any USB drive attached to an infected host and masquerades as folders to trick users into propagating the infection sideways.

name: Process Discovery
usage: IXESHE backdoor enumerates the process list on victim hosts to identify security software and running applications before staging further activity.

name: Dynamic Resolution: Domain Generation Algorithms
usage: Signature DynCalc / DNSCalc technique - operators encode C2 IPv4 octets inside numeric fields of DNS answers so implants can compute their next callback address without a firmware update.

name: Data Encoding: Standard Encoding
usage: Etumbot, HIGHTIDE and WATERSPOUT base64-encode command output and file transfers inside HTTP request bodies and query strings to blend into web traffic.

name: Deliver Malicious App via Other Means (Mobile)
usage: Android side of operations: Firestarter and Tanzeem installed via social-engineering links, and, per Cyfirma, occasional trafficking through Google Play under fake chat-app branding.

name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Device Administrator Permissions (Mobile)
usage: Tanzeem and Firestarter request Android Accessibility Services and Device Admin so they can silently harvest SMS, call logs, contacts, GPS and take screen recordings.

name: Protected User Data: SMS Messages (Mobile)
usage: StealJob, Firestarter and Tanzeem collect SMS content, call logs and contacts once Accessibility Services / SMS permissions are granted.

name: Brute Force
usage: AA20-296A documented password-spray and brute-force attempts against exposed Outlook Web Access, RDP and Citrix portals of US SLTT targets.

name: Compromise Infrastructure: Server
usage: Compromises web servers that host software updates, then uses them as delivery infrastructure for MgBot and Nightdoor drops against Tibetan and China-domestic targets.

name: Masquerading: Rename Legitimate Utilities
usage: Renames rundll32.exe (e.g. to dbengin.exe inside ProgramData\Microsoft\PlayReady) to proxy MgBot loader DLL execution while blending into signed-utility footprints.

name: Steal Web Session Cookie
usage: CloudScout .NET modules read Chrome and Edge cookie stores to lift live session tokens for Google Drive, Gmail and Outlook Web mailboxes of compromised users.

name: Query Registry
usage: Uses reg.exe to enumerate Security Account Manager, System and Security hives during post-exploitation profiling of Windows victims.

name: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Golden Ticket
usage: Secureworks CTU observed Tick forging Kerberos golden tickets after harvesting KRBTGT hashes, granting the operators long-term domain-level persistence.

name: Software Extensions: Browser Extensions
usage: LONGTALE / GemStone Chrome extension masquerading as Google Gemini, installed by tampering the Secure Preferences file.

name: Execution Guardrails
usage: BlueMoon loader gates on User-Agent and OS; p2 rejects any Windows build outside a specific set (17763, 19041-19045, 20348, 22000).

name: Phishing: Spearphishing Voice
usage: Signature technique. Voice calls to IT help desks impersonating employees to obtain password/MFA resets. Unit 42 reports >70% of 2025 numbers used Google Voice VoIP; help-desk verification answers pre-scripted from earlier OSINT.

name: Multi-Factor Authentication Request Generation
usage: MFA-fatigue / push-bombing. Repeatedly triggers Duo/Authenticator push notifications until the victim approves one, often paired with a vishing call framing the pushes as a legitimate 'sync issue'.

name: SIM Card Swap
usage: Historical bread-and-butter (Star Fraud era). Bribes or social-engineers telco employees to port the victim's number to an attacker-controlled SIM, intercepting SMS OTPs. Basis of the Urban / Buchanan indictments.

name: Modify Authentication Process: Multi-Factor Authentication
usage: After account takeover, registers attacker-controlled MFA tokens on the victim account so subsequent access no longer requires social engineering â the standard identity-first persistence primitive.

name: Modify Authentication Process: Conditional Access Policies
usage: Adds attacker IP ranges / geolocations to Azure AD conditional access 'trusted locations' to exempt itself from step-up MFA policies while remaining below the radar of anomaly rules.

name: Domain or Tenant Policy Modification: Trust Modification
usage: Adds rogue federated identity providers to Microsoft Entra ID (Golden SAML). Enables the operator to mint arbitrary user tokens against the tenant without knowing any password.

name: Email Collection: Email Forwarding Rule
usage: Creates inbox rules that auto-delete or hide security/IT alert emails (Duo, Okta, EDR, MFA change notifications) sent to the compromised user during the intrusion â closes the victim's own detection loop.

name: Service Stop
usage: Terminates SQL Server, Exchange, backup-agent and hypervisor services before encryption to unlock files for the encryptor thread.

name: Defacement: Internal Defacement
usage: Rewrites the desktop wallpaper and drops readme.txt ransom notes in every encrypted directory; leak-site listing on Basta News completes the extortion loop.
